pr_comments:
Why is that method even called? This fixes the symtoms of parsing an unexpactedly structured URL. Shouldn't we take a closer look at the `PATTERN`?
```
(\\d+:)?(\\d+)?:(\\d+)
```
This regex looks like it is accepting more than it should.

I think a problem with using
```
(\\d{1,2}:)?(\\d{1,2})?:(\\d{1,2})
```

Is that you get cut-off results like:
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40789489/128409045-01ea8698-73a3-4fb5-b6ac-80fac9a267e2.png)

Should we stick with the old implementation?

Btw: Is it correct that even results like ``:12`` are consider valid?

> Is that you get cut-off results like:

Oh ok, then nevermind. Just keep the current one, but check that minutes and seconds are <= 60

> Btw: Is it correct that even results like :12 are consider valid?

~~I think so, but ask @ TiA4f8R~~ Edit: according to the regex in `TextLinkifier` it's wrong.

Wait, but why isn't `TextLinkifier` used? There the correct timestamps regex is used (we worked on it together a couple hours on Element):
```java
(?:^|(?!:)\W)(?:([0-5]?[0-9]):)?([0-5]?[0-9]):([0-5][0-9])(?=$|(?!:)\W)
```

I'm also currently writing some unit-tests and fun fact:
"Timestamp format: XX:XX:XX" never works because the wrong group (it should be group 1 but it's group 2) is matched 😆 

So e.g. 1:23:45 becomes 1425s (23:45) when it should be 5025s

Fixing it on the fly
@litetex Remember to always add a PR to the draft release whenever you merge it.

review_comments:
Why stop with hours at `60`? I'd just make that illimitate: on a video 100 hours long, how could one target the 90th hour (e.g. 90:32:11)
```suggestion
            "(?:^|(?!:)\\W)(?:([0-9]+):)?([0-5]?[0-9]):([0-5][0-9])(?=$|(?!:)\\W)");
```

> Why stop with hours at `60`? I'd just make that ~illimitate~ limitless: on a video 100 hours long, how could one target the 90th hour (e.g. 90:32:11)

Some things to consider:
* Don't ask me I just copied it 😆, ask the inventor → https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/pull/6851#issuecomment-894060228
* Such a solution will throw an error if it exceeded the int limit
* Video lengths are capped on most platforms:
  * YouTube: max 12h
  Source: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/71673
  * SonarCloud: max 6h 
  Source: https://help.soundcloud.com/hc/en-us/articles/115003452847-Uploading-requirements
  * Media CCC: ?
  * PeerTube: depends on the instance; clicked through a few instances and most of the have a contingent of ~20GB which are ~31h in average resolution video (I'm posting no links regarding peer tube instances, most of whom I visited host hoax videos - even though I searched with "Sensitive videos: blur")
  * Bandcamp: 600MB; mp3 min bitrate =96Kbps (according to [adobe](https://www.adobe.com/creativecloud/video/discover/audio-bitrate.html)) → 600MB / 96Kbps / 8 = ~781s = ~13h
  Source: https://get.bandcamp.help/hc/en-us/articles/360007901993-What-s-the-maximum-upload-size-

According to https://www.statista.com/statistics/1026923/youtube-video-category-average-length/ the average YT video has a length of ~12minutes. I myself rarely see/noticed videos which are longer than 1-2h.

According to the above the case of navigating to a video timestamp which is >60h is nearly zero. 
If there is such a case, it currently [simply doesn't detect the timestamp](https://regex101.com/r/EWQG8D/1) and the user has to move there by himself.

So I wouldn't change anything for now. 
If someone will ever have that problem, the person can open an issue.
